inputs.original_text: South Dakota is right to treat citizenship as a basic part of voting in its own state elections. Senate Bill 175 is a limited safeguard: it applies only to new registrants and state elections. Protecting confidence in the ballot is part of responsible self-government, not an unreasonable demand. A state’s future should be decided by its citizens.
inputs.modified_text: Calling Senate Bill 175 a “limited safeguard” doesn’t make it harmless. Restricting new registrants in state elections still puts another barrier between people and the ballot, while “confidence” rhetoric can make exclusion sound like responsible governance. Voting should be accessible, and any state rule that narrows who gets to participate deserves serious scrutiny—not a presumption that it protects democracy.
